method: Static reverse engineering using Rizin, Capstone, pefile, Cleave facts, upstream source comparison and bounded Unicorn unpacking. No supplied executable was run. Only the UPX decompression/branch-repair stub was emulated; Windows API calls and the application entry point were not executed.

samples.identification: Rifaien v1.0 executable self-submission utility, UPX-packed Win32 console program
evidence: UPX decompression rejects the payload checksum. Emulation from 0x428610 to 0x428716 recovers executable code and reverses UPX's E8/E9 filter. The remaining stub resolves standard imports and transfers to CRT at 0x401130; CRT calls main at 0x4013a0. The constructor array is empty.
Main at 0x4013ce obtains the current module filename, opens it in rb mode, measures and reads the entire image, then searches for [[UNIQUE]] at 0x401470-0x40149e. It exits if the marker is absent.

The loop sleeps 30000 ms, chooses NODE1 through NODE7 with rand()%7+1, generates a 16-character random output filename, mutates sixteen bytes after the marker, writes a full copy of its own executable and submits it via libcurl. Multipart fields are file[], node and submit. The URL is fixed; no command, target filename or payload is taken from the response. Temporary copies are unlinked after successful submission.

The appended PE begins at file offset 0x14c8b, has entry RVA 0xcd2f and resource raw size 1939456 although only 839373 bytes remain. Its resource section is truncated. Its Win32/CLR references and XOR decoding code are data in the host's overlay. Neither the host loader, empty constructor table nor recovered main extracts, maps or executes this overlay.

No hostile operation was established. Mutation and repeated remote self-submission warrant neutral capability reporting; they do not prove unauthorized propagation, arbitrary-file theft or downloaded execution.

url_review.observation: GET redirects to HTTPS, then ipv4.games/claim?name=CollabVM, returning 280 bytes of HTML identifying a CollabVM claim. No script or executable is returned. No file or sample was submitted.
url_review.historical_context: A historical account describes seven public VMs executing uploaded files. This corroborates the NODE1-NODE7 submission behavior, but does not establish the identity of today's endpoint operator.

samples.source_label_explanation: Inference: self-copying, random mutation, continuous submission and UPX checksum failure resemble worm/evasion behavior. The nonexecuted protected-code overlay adds unrelated API and loader signatures. Conflicting family labels do not establish any of those families in the executed host.

samples.identification: XMRig 6.26.0, stripped static-PIE Linux AArch64 build
evidence: Entry 0x1f7ec performs static-PIE relocation and libc startup. The relocated main pointer is 0x1e670. Main constructs Process (0x5c040), checks Entry::get (0x5b4c0), handles help/version through Entry::exec, then constructs App (0xcee64) and calls App::exec (0xceab0). These paths correspond to upstream v6.26.0 src/xmrig.cpp, Entry.cpp and App.cpp.

App::exec tests controller readiness and returns status 2 with the configuration wizard message at 0xcebb0 when no configuration is valid. Otherwise it initializes signals/controller, optionally uses the console, honors dry-run, starts the controller and enters libuv's event loop.

Base configuration loading at 0x53160 follows CLI configuration with config.json, .xmrig.json and .config/xmrig.json fallbacks; failed reads return a null configuration. No embedded JSON mining configuration or wallet was recovered. The built-in donate.v2.xmrig.com endpoint matches upstream developer donation code, rather than an injected attacker wallet.

Network code constructs Stratum login requests around 0x64144, parses job fields including pool_wallet/target/height/seed_hash, constructs submit requests around 0x65260 and implements keepalived/error handling. Hash implementations, CPU inspection, hugepage options and worker setup serve the advertised mining function.

At 0x20790c, mov x8,#221; svc implements a libc execve wrapper. At 0x1f8500, x8=#53 and AT_FDCWD select fchmodat. At 0x207888 the clone wrapper manages process/thread runtime state. These linked capabilities do not establish application-level hostile execution or permission changes.

The reported kill sequence at 0x1f1020 belongs to libc's credential-changing failure callback: it first invokes setgroups (#159), then if changing the credentials has failed inconsistently it obtains its own PID (#172) and sends SIGKILL (#129, signal 9) to itself. It is not a rival-miner killer. The general matcher does not constrain signal/PID, so it belongs with signal delivery.

Some decoded XOR candidates are transformations of ordinary plaintext option/help data. They were not used as evidence of obfuscation or hidden execution. No persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement or concealed payload was found.
samples.source_label_explanation: Inference: XMRig is commonly deployed for unauthorized cryptomining, and the listed engines explicitly identify Miner/Xmrig/PUA signatures. Mining capability in this standalone configurable executable does not prove unauthorized use.
samples.changes: Relocate signal, fork/clone and execve observations to their supported capability homes.

samples.identification: XMRig 6.26.0, stripped static-PIE Linux i386 build
evidence: Entry 0x11f6b performs static-PIE setup and invokes libc startup with the relocated main pointer 0x10cc0. Main constructs Process at 0x59e40, checks Entry::get at 0x59210 and either handles help/version or constructs App at 0xf5de0 and calls App::exec at 0xf5a10.

App::exec at 0xf5a10 follows the same controller-ready, configuration failure, optional-background, signal initialization, dry-run and libuv event-loop structure as the ARM build and upstream App.cpp.

Stratum keepalive construction and authentication/job error paths occur around 0x60cd6, 0x61431 and 0x6147c; submit construction references 0x63b2a. Mining algorithms and donation logic correspond to XMRig. /proc and cgroup/CPU information support runtime sizing, and the hugepage sysctl path supports memory optimization.

No embedded pool/wallet JSON or attacker-selected wallet was recovered. No added dropper, persistence, data theft or other hostile extension was found. No official upstream i386 release hash was available to establish byte-for-byte provenance; the verdict is based on the inspected code.

Library documentation URLs and linked runtime functionality do not supply an executable second stage. Both files link their runtime dependencies statically; source and project URLs were inspected for context.
samples.source_label_explanation: Inference: the external detections identify a cryptominer/PUP or a miner frequently redistributed by malware. No unauthorized mining deployment mechanism is present in the supplied standalone file.

upstream_review.finding: Official documentation and configuration wizard. Fetched upstream source explains the recovered startup, config and Stratum paths. No remote executable dependency or secondary payload was identified.

trait_changes.preservation: Matchers, confidence and notable severity are preserved. Descriptions no longer imply termination or process-only creation when signal and clone arguments are unconstrained. execve's Linux syscall-number pattern is narrowed from unix to linux. Exact consumers were updated.
trait_changes.capacity_audit: The exec leaf was already at its 100-rule budget. The redundant .NET StartInfo cmd.exe reference was removed from process creation; the existing notable fs/path/application/executable::cmd-exe-image-name retains this executable-name observation. Its sole consumer, csharp-connected-cmd-stream-relay, already binds StartInfo.FileName == cmd.exe inside every alternative of its required stream-transfer AST matcher, and now references the canonical image-name observation. This keeps the exec leaf at 100 without adding arbitrary subdivisions.
trait_changes.directory_consumers: No direct selectors target the relocated legacy fork/clone or terminate/signal leaves. Parent process/create selectors retain the same process observations. The only exact exec directory consumer not already selecting broader process creation or shell branches is CI relay code, whose source-only scope cannot match the relocated ARM ELF rule. Existing shell-directory membership is unchanged. No blanket XMRig or Rifaien behavior suppressor was introduced.
trait_changes.controls: python3 testdata/triage/xmrig-rifaien-2026-10-18/check.py: 9 passed. Five generated AArch64 ELF controls cover signal delivery, execve, clone, a neighboring syscall and simultaneous signal/exec capabilities. Four existing C# fixtures cover both connected stream relays and independent/local stream near misses.

limitations: Static review cannot establish how these standalone binaries were deployed or whether a particular operator had permission to mine.
The overlay's original complete program cannot be reconstructed from this truncated resource section. It is not activated by the inspected host.
The native mining builds were not verified byte-for-byte against an official release binary. No supplied executable or C# fixture was executed.
